chunks: When she heard their slanderings, she sent for them and prepared a banquet, and gave each of them a knife, and called (to Joseph): 'Come out before them.' When they saw him, the women were so wonderstruck they cut their hands, and exclaimed: 'O Lord preserve us! He is no mortal but an honourable angel.'

key_terms.حَاشَ لِلَّهِ: O Lord preserve us/Glory to God

ai.seo_question: Why did the women of Egypt cut their hands when they saw Joseph?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this scene highlights Joseph's divine beauty (Jamal) as a physical manifestation of his spiritual purity, often linked to the concept of 'Nur' (light). The women's self-inflicted wounds symbolize their overwhelming awe and the transcendence of worldly perception when confronted with a divinely favored figure. This event serves as a testament to his prophetic status even before his explicit mission, reinforcing the theme of divine selection in the Quranic narrative.
